Background

Rebuilding after two storms

The Mylestom tidal pool took a battering in 2025 — first from Tropical Cyclone Alfred in March, then the NSW East Coast severe weather event in May. Between the two, the pool's marine piles, decking and shark-net enclosure were damaged badly enough that Bellingen Shire Council needed more than a patch-up: a proper resilience rebuild, done before the next season of storms.

Scope of works

What we rebuilt

Replaced five damaged marine piles

Installed new fibreglass mesh decking

Replaced the shark net enclosure & stainless-steel bracings

Added new bench seats & bollards

Installed a debris boom to manage driftwood through the pool enclosure

Funding

How it was funded

Boating Infrastructure Emergency Repair Pool (BIERP)$269,515.32
Crown Reserves Improvement Funding (CRIF)$246,575.00
Bellingen Shire Council (S7.12 Developer contribution)$140,082.00
Total project value$656,172.32

On site

Progress & completion

The tidal pool is open to the community again, with new piles, decking, enclosure and driftwood management in place ahead of the next storm season.
